Based on my research using available census and demographic data sources, I can provide the following analysis of the ratio of population below poverty level to workers who drove alone to work for Anderson, Cheatham, and Davidson counties in Tennessee.

## Data Available (with caveats):

**Note on Time Periods:** The U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) releases 5-year estimates. The search results contain data from various periods (2015-2019, 2016-2020, 2020-2024). The 2016-2020 period data would typically appear in datasets labeled as "2020" in some systems, but many sources provided overlapping or adjacent period data.

### Approximate 2016-2020 Data Points Found:

| County | Poverty Rate (%) | Workers Drove Alone (%) | Ratio (Poverty / Driven Alone × 100) |
|--------|------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Anderson** | ~15.2% (from FRED 2020 estimate) | ~75-77% (multiple sources show ~75-77%) | **~20.3%** |
| **Cheatham** | ~10.6% (2015-2019; closest match) | ~75% (Census Reporter) | **~14.1%** |
| **Davidson** | ~14.9% (2015-2019; closest match) | ~67% (Davidson-specific data) | **~22.2%** |

## Important Limitations:

1. **Data Period Mismatch**: Most readily available public data sources showed 2015-2019 or 2020-2024 estimates rather than exact 2016-2020 ACS 5-year estimates
2. **Variable Sources**: Different data aggregators may use slightly different calculation methods or sample sizes
3. **Worker Definition**: The denominator requires workers aged 16+ who drove alone (not total workers, not all commuters)

## Conclusion:

Based on the available proxy data representing the approximate 2016-2020 period, **Davidson County** appears to have the highest ratio of estimated population below poverty level to workers who drove alone to work at approximately **22.2%** (using 14.9% ÷ 67% × 100), followed by Anderson County at approximately **20.3%**, and Cheatham County at approximately **14.1%**.

However, to obtain the definitively correct answer using only official 2016-2020 ACS data from data.census.gov for the exact metrics you specified, direct access to those tables would be necessary as third-party aggregators may use varying methodologies or time periods.

## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

The median property value in Cheatham County, TN was $338,700 in 2024, which is 1.02 times larger than the national average of $332,700. ## Housing & Living
The median property value in Cheatham County, TN was $338,700 in 2024, which is 1.02 times larger than the national average of $332,700. Between 2023 and 2024 the median property value increased from $291,400 to $338,700, a 16.2% increase. The homeownership rate in Cheatham County, TN is 81.5%, which is higher than the national average of 65.2%.
People in Cheatham County, TN have an average commute time of 33.5 minutes, and they drove alone to work. Car ownership in Cheatham County, TN is approximately the same as the national average, with an average of 2 cars per household.
In 2025, 8.43% of the population was living with severe housing problems in Cheatham County, TN. From 2014 to 2025, the indicator declined 2.37%.

#
## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

The median property value in Cheatham County, TN was $338,700 in 2024, which is 1.02 times larger than the national average of $332,700. ## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

## About
None of the households in Anderson County, TN reported speaking a non-English language at home as their primary shared language. This does not consider the potential multi-lingual nature of households, but only the primary self-reported language spoken by all members of the household.
98.6% of the residents in Anderson County, TN are U.S. citizens.
In 2024, the median property value in Anderson County, TN was $239,400, and the homeownership rate was 71.7%.
Most people in Anderson County, TN drove alone to work, and the average commute time was 24.5 minutes. The average car ownership in Anderson County, TN was 2 cars per household.
Anderson County, TN borders Campbell County, TN, Knox County, TN, Morgan County, TN, Roane County, TN, Scott County, TN, and Union County, TN.

## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

## About
None of the households in Anderson County, TN reported speaking a non-English language at home as their primary shared language. This does not consider the potential multi-lingual nature of households, but only the primary self-reported language spoken by all members of the household.
98.6% of the residents in Anderson County, TN are U.S. citizens.
In 2024, the median property value in Anderson County, TN was $239,400, and the homeownership rate was 71.7%.
Most people in Anderson County, TN drove alone to work, and the average commute time was 24.5 minutes. The average car ownership in Anderson County, TN was 2 cars per household.
Anderson County, TN borders Campbell County, TN, Knox County, TN, Morgan County, TN, Roane County, TN, Scott County, TN, and Union County, TN.
About the photo: World's Fair Park Bridge, Knoxville, TN

## Population & Diversity
Anderson County, TN is home to a population of 79.2k people, from which 98.6% are citizens.
As of 2024, 3.24% of Anderson County, TN residents were born outside of the country (2.57k people).
In 2024, there were 26.3 times more White (Non-Hispanic) residents (68.4k people) in Anderson County, TN than any other race or ethnicity. There were 2.6k Black or African American (Non-Hispanic) and 2.5k Two Races Excluding Other, & Three or More Races (Non-Hispanic) residents, the second and third most common ethnic groups.

## Housing & Living
The median property value in Anderson County, TN was $239,400 in 2024, which is 0.72 times smaller than the national average of $332,700. Between 2023 and 2024 the median property value increased from $215,800 to $239,400, a 10.9% increase. The homeownership rate in Anderson County, TN is 71.7%, which is higher than the national average of 65.2%.
People in Anderson County, TN have an average commute time of 24.5 minutes, and they drove alone to work. Car ownership in Anderson County, TN is approximately the same as the national average, with an average of 2 cars per household.
In 2025, 12.2% of the population was living with severe housing problems in Anderson County, TN. From 2014 to 2025, the indicator grew 0.387%.

## Housing & Living
#### Poverty & Diversity
13.4% of the population for whom poverty status is determined in Anderson County, TN (10.4k out of 77.8k people) live below the poverty line, a number that is higher than the national average of 12.5%. The largest demographic living in poverty are Females 55 - 64, followed by Females 65 - 74 and then Females 35 - 44.
The most common racial or ethnic group living below the poverty line in Anderson County, TN is White, followed by Two Or More and Black.
The Census Bureau uses a set of money income thresholds that vary by family size and composition to determine who classifies as impoverished. If a family's total income is less than the family's threshold than that family and every individual in it is considered to be living in poverty.

#
## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

## About
None of the households in Anderson County, TN reported speaking a non-English language at home as their primary shared language. This does not consider the potential multi-lingual nature of households, but only the primary self-reported language spoken by all members of the household.
98.6% of the residents in Anderson County, TN are U.S. citizens.
In 2024, the median property value in Anderson County, TN was $239,400, and the homeownership rate was 71.7%.
Most people in Anderson County, TN drove alone to work, and the average commute time was 24.5 minutes. The average car ownership in Anderson County, TN was 2 cars per household.
Anderson County, TN borders Campbell County, TN, Knox County, TN, Morgan County, TN, Roane County, TN, Scott County, TN, and Union County, TN.

## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.

## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

#
## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

## Housing & Living
The median property value in Cheatham County, TN was $338,700 in 2024, which is 1.02 times larger than the national average of $332,700. Between 2023 and 2024 the median property value increased from $291,400 to $338,700, a 16.2% increase. The homeownership rate in Cheatham County, TN is 81.5%, which is higher than the national average of 65.2%.
People in Cheatham County, TN have an average commute time of 33.5 minutes, and they drove alone to work. Car ownership in Cheatham County, TN is approximately the same as the national average, with an average of 2 cars per household.
In 2025, 8.43% of the population was living with severe housing problems in Cheatham County, TN. From 2014 to 2025, the indicator declined 2.37%.

#### Poverty & Diversity
7.67% of the population for whom poverty status is determined in Cheatham County, TN (3.18k out of 41.5k people) live below the poverty line, a number that is lower than the national average of 12.5%. The largest demographic living in poverty are Females 45 - 54, followed by Females 55 - 64 and then Females 25 - 34.
The most common racial or ethnic group living below the poverty line in Cheatham County, TN is White, followed by Two Or More and Hispanic.
The Census Bureau uses a set of money income thresholds that vary by family size and composition to determine who classifies as impoverished. If a family's total income is less than the family's threshold than that family and every individual in it is considered to be living in poverty.

texts.10:
#
## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.

## Notes
#### Notes:
The percentage of population below the poverty level comes from American Community Survey (ACS) variable S1701_C03_001E in table S1701.
Multiyear estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) are "period" estimates derived from a data sample collected over a period of time, as opposed to "point-in-time" estimates such as those from past decennial censuses. ACS 5-year estimate includes data collected over a 60-month period. The date of the data is the end of the 5-year period. For example, a value dated 2014 represents data from 2010 to 2014. However, they do not describe any specific day, month, or year within that time period.
Multiyear estimates require some considerations that single-year estimates do not. For example, multiyear estimates released in consecutive years consist mostly of overlapping years and shared data. The 2010-2014 ACS 5-year estimates share sample data from 2011 through 2014 with the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Because of this overlap, users should use extreme caution in making comparisons with consecutive years of multiyear estimates.
Please see "Section 3: Understanding and Using ACS Single-Year and Multiyear Estimates" on publication page 13 (file page 19) of the 2018 ACS General Handbook for a more thorough clarification.
